fields.h1: Build Interview Scheduling Automation That Books Every Round
fields.hero_description: Build interview scheduling automation that lets candidates book their own slot and covers a declined interview with a backup.
fields.features_heading: What Your Interview Scheduling App Handles
fields.features_subheading: Each interview is booked from the right pool of interviewers, at a time every person on it can make.
fields.feature_1:
Trained interviewers for each round

List who can run each round, such as system design. The app picks only from that list and reads each person's busy hours from Google Calendar or Microsoft 365 first.
fields.feature_2:
Booking links in the candidate's time zone

Candidates pick from open slots shown in their own local time, and the invite lands on both calendars with a video link. Nobody on your team converts a time by hand.
fields.feature_3:
Loops ordered around the tightest calendar

The app books the interviewer with the narrowest free window first, then fits the rest of the loop around that slot. The candidate gets one itinerary with every name.
fields.feature_4:
Declines covered from the same pool

When an interviewer declines, the app moves the invite to another trained interviewer free at that time. If nobody is free, the recruiter gets a Slack or email alert.
fields.feature_5:
A weekly cap on interviews per person

Set the number of interviews each person can take in a week. A live dashboard shows every count, and the app skips anyone at the cap when it assigns the next request.
fields.feature_6:
Every booking kept in a database you own

Each invite, decline, and swap is saved with its time and the person who made it, in a database you own. Export the app's full code to your GitHub repo on paid plans.

fields.usecase_heading: Where Interview Logistics Slip Without Rules
fields.tab_content_1:
6 open slots, each shown in her own time zone

Tamsin Oduya moves billing specialist Ifeoma Castellanos to phone screen at Wrenfield Dental Partners. The app emails Ifeoma 6 open 30-minute slots over the next 5 business days, in Mountain Time. She picks Wednesday at 9:30 AM, and the call lands on Tamsin's calendar at 11:30 AM Eastern with a video link.
fields.tab_content_2:
With the manager free only after 1:00 PM, she goes last

Corvane Robotics needs 4 interviews of 45 minutes each for Mateus Lindqvist, a firmware engineer in the final round. The hiring manager, Ottilie Brandvold, is free only after 1:00 PM. The app books 10:00 AM to 1:45 PM with 15-minute breaks and puts her interview last. Mateus gets one itinerary with all 4.
fields.tab_content_3:
When Desmond declines, Noor takes his 2:00 PM slot

Desmond Achterberg declines Elspeth Marchetti's Thursday 2:00 PM interview at Ashgrove Credit Union 20 hours ahead. Jarrah Whitcombe and Lorcan Pettigrew, also trained for it, are busy then, so the app hands the slot to Noor Halloran. Elspeth keeps her time and gets an updated invite with Noor's name on it.
fields.tab_content_4:
No one runs more than 3 interviews a week

Marrowgate Software trained 5 engineers to run its system design interview and caps each at 3 interviews a week. Rufus Calloway already has 3 this week, so when the next candidate books, the app skips him. The interview goes to Wilhelmina Osei, who had none, and her count on the dashboard moves to 1.

fields.howto_description: Seven steps to plan interview scheduling automation around your rounds and interviewers, then build it and book one real candidate.
fields.howto_step_2_title: 02 Name who can run each round
fields.howto_step_4_title: 04 Describe the app in a prompt
fields.howto_step_1_des: Write down each round you book, with its length and who takes part. Note which rounds a candidate books alone and which need several interviewers on the same day.
fields.howto_step_2_des: For each round, list the interviewers trained to run it and the hours they will interview. Set a weekly cap for each person now, before the same few people end up on every loop.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Connect Google Calendar or Microsoft 365 for every interviewer, plus your applicant tracking system if it has an API. Pick the stage change that sends a candidate a booking link.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Tell Emergent the rounds, the interviewer lists, the caps, and the booking window in plain English. Ask for a dashboard of interviews per person, and change any rule later by prompting.
fields.howto_step_5_title: 05 Decide what happens on a decline
fields.howto_step_5_des: Have the app try the trained interviewers first and alert the recruiter only when none of them is free. Set how many times a candidate can move an interview before a recruiter steps in.
fields.howto_step_6_des: Draft the booking email, the confirmation, and a reminder for the day before. Put the interviewer names and the video link in every message. A candidate with both has no reason to email the recruiter.
fields.howto_step_7_des: Run one candidate from your pipeline through every round on real calendars. Check that each invite shows the right time zone and that a test decline reaches a trained backup before the whole team uses it.

faq_plan.a: Interview scheduling automation is software that offers candidates open times from your interviewers' calendars and books the one they pick. It also handles the logistics a coordinator would chase by email, such as ordering a panel loop or covering an interview when someone declines. A recruiter steps in only when the rules cannot find a time.

faq_plan.q: How do I set up interview scheduling automation?
faq_plan.a: Write down each interview round, who is trained to run it, and how many interviews each person can take a week. Then describe those rounds and limits in a prompt in Emergent's AI automation builder. Emergent builds the scheduling app with its database and dashboard. Connect your calendars through their APIs, and test the app on one candidate first.

faq_plan.q: What should I look for in interview scheduling automation tools beyond a booking link?
faq_plan.a: Look at the cases a booking link does not cover. Check whether the tool can book several interviewers back to back on one day, replace an interviewer who declines, and cap how many interviews one person takes a week. With Emergent, those rules live in an app you describe in a prompt, and every booking is stored in a database you own.

faq_plan.q: Should interview scheduling automation be separate from the rest of hiring automation?
faq_plan.a: Yes, it works well as its own app, and it is a good first piece because its rules are about calendars, not judgment. Screening applicants, stage deadlines, and offers belong to recruitment automation, which can hand a candidate to the scheduler at the stage change. Keep one candidate record shared by both, with every reschedule next to the interview notes.

faq_plan.q: How should interview scheduling automation handle candidates in other time zones?
faq_plan.a: Store every slot in one standard time and convert it only when you show it. The candidate sees times in their own zone, each interviewer sees theirs, and the invite names the zone. Build the booking window from the interviewer's working hours, then drop any slot that falls before 8:00 AM or after 6:00 PM for the candidate.

faq_plan.q: How many time slots should interview scheduling automation offer a candidate?
faq_plan.a: Offer about 6, spread across at least 3 different days. Include an early and a late option for candidates who work a day job. If the candidate has not booked within 48 hours, send one reminder with fresh times, and tell the recruiter after a second day with no booking.

faq_plan.q: How do staffing agencies use interview scheduling automation with clients?
faq_plan.a: Give each client's hiring managers their own pool in the app, with calendars connected or open hours entered by hand when a client will not share a calendar. The candidate books from those hours, and the agency recruiter is copied on every invite. When a new client signs, collect its interviewers and hours in your client onboarding workflow.

faq_plan.q: How do I add new interviewers to interview scheduling automation?
faq_plan.a: Add them as shadows first, booked onto real interviews as an extra seat. After 2 or 3 shadow sessions, switch them to reverse shadow, where they lead and a trained interviewer watches. Then move them into the pool with the same weekly cap as everyone else. In an app Emergent builds, that switch is one prompt, and each interviewer's status sits in a database you own.

faq_plan.q: What should interview scheduling automation do when a candidate misses an interview?
faq_plan.a: Have the interviewer mark a no-show in the app after 10 minutes, and let the app send the candidate one new booking link with fresh times. A second no-show should close the booking and alert the recruiter instead of offering more times. Record each no-show on the candidate record, since a pattern by time of day points to a fix in your reminders.

faq_plan.q: Can interview scheduling automation arrange travel for onsite interviews?
faq_plan.a: It can start the request, but leave the booking itself with whoever handles travel. Once a loop is booked, have the app send the travel coordinator the candidate's name and the travel dates. If your finance team needs a purchase order before travel is booked, route that request through purchase order automation instead of email.

plan.angle: Searchers for interview scheduling automation want the back-and-forth gone, and roundups of booking tools stop at a link that shows open times. This page covers the logistics around that link: candidates who book a phone screen in their own time zone, a 4-interview loop ordered around the one interviewer with a narrow window, a backup swapped in when an interviewer declines the day before, and a weekly cap that spreads interviews across the trained pool. Screening, stage clocks and offers stay with the recruitment automation page, and general meeting booking and meeting hours stay with the calendar automation page.
